subject: September 11 attacks
overview: The **September 11 attacks** (9/11) were four coordinated suicide hijackings carried out on the morning of **September 11, 2001**, by 19 **al-Qaeda** terrorists targeting symbols of American economic, military, and political power. Two airliners struck and brought down the Twin Towers of the **World Trade Center** in New York City, a third hit the **Pentagon**, and a fourth—**United Airlines Flight 93**—crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers and crew revolted. Killing **2,977 victims** from 90 nations, the attacks triggered the U.S.-led invasion of Afghanistan, sweeping counterterrorism laws, and a lasting transformation of global security and aviation.

key_moments.title: The Twin Towers Struck and Collapse
key_moments.text: Hijacked **American Airlines Flight 11** slammed into floors 93 to 99 of the World Trade Center’s North Tower at 8:46 a.m., followed 17 minutes later by **United Airlines Flight 175** striking floors 77 to 85 of the South Tower. Though most of the 16,400 to 18,000 people in the complex evacuated safely while first responders rushed inside, structural damage and jet-fuel fires brought down both towers and destroyed the five other buildings in the complex, killing **2,753 people** in New York.

key_moments.title: Strike on the Pentagon and Ground Stop
key_moments.text: A third hijacked airliner, **American Airlines Flight 77** out of Washington Dulles, crashed into the west wall of the **Pentagon** in Arlington, Virginia, killing **184 victims** (59 passengers and crew aboard the jet plus 125 people inside the building). Eight minutes later, at 9:45 a.m., the Federal Aviation Administration ordered all airborne civilian aircraft across the United States to land immediately—the first nationwide ground stop in U.S. aviation history.

key_moments.title: The Flight 93 Passenger Revolt
key_moments.text: Delayed more than 25 minutes on the ground in Newark, **United Airlines Flight 93** was hijacked around 9:28 a.m. and turned toward Washington, D.C.—likely targeting the U.S. Capitol. Through airfone calls, the 33 passengers and 7 crew members learned of the World Trade Center strikes and voted to rush the cockpit. As they fought to break in, the hijackers pitched and rolled the jet upside down and crashed it into a field in Somerset County, Pennsylvania, killing all 40 victims aboard but sparing the capital.

key_moments.title: Global Response, Afghanistan, and Security Overhaul
key_moments.text: NATO invoked its collective defense clause (**Article 5**), and after Afghanistan’s Taliban regime refused President **George W. Bush’s** demand to surrender al-Qaeda leaders and close training camps, the U.S. launched **Operation Enduring Freedom** on October 7, 2001. At home and abroad, governments passed sweeping counterterrorism laws—including the **USA Patriot Act**—created the U.S. **Department of Homeland Security**, reinforced airliner cockpits, and assigned sky marshals to flights.

deep_facts.text: With subways halted and Hudson tunnels closed after the Twin Towers collapsed, hundreds of thousands of trapped office workers, residents, and students fled to Lower Manhattan’s seawall. Answering a U.S. Coast Guard call for **“all available boats,”** an improvised flotilla of ferries, tugboats, charter boats, fireboats, and private vessels evacuated an estimated **300,000 to 500,000 people** to New Jersey and Brooklyn in **under nine hours**—the largest waterborne evacuation in American history.

When the FAA shut down U.S. airspace at 9:45 a.m., roughly **4,500 planes** landed safely across the country—while hundreds of transatlantic and transpacific jets still in the air had nowhere to go. Under **Operation Yellow Ribbon**, Canada closed its own airspace for the first time and absorbed **225 to 240 diverted airliners** across 17 airports; tiny **Gander, Newfoundland**, alone took in **38 wide-body jets** carrying 6,122 passengers and 473 crew until U.S. skies reopened.

In October 2001, recovery workers pulled a badly burned 8-foot **Callery pear tree** with snapped roots and a single living branch from the Ground Zero rubble. Nursed back to health at a Bronx parks nursery—where it even bounced back after a storm uprooted it in March 2010—the **Survivor Tree** returned to the 9/11 Memorial in **December 2010** standing 30 feet tall, its smooth new limbs visibly growing out of gnarled, scarred stumps.

connections.name: Osama bin Laden
connections.connection: The founder and leader of al-Qaeda directed the terrorist network behind the September 11 attacks before being killed in a U.S. military operation on May 1, 2011.

connections.name: George W. Bush
connections.connection: The U.S. president declared that nations harboring terrorists would be treated as hostile regimes, launching the war in Afghanistan and the broader post-9/11 security overhaul.

connections.name: War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)
connections.connection: Launched on October 7, 2001, as Operation Enduring Freedom after the Taliban refused to hand over al-Qaeda leaders based in Afghanistan.

connections.name: Iraq War
connections.connection: Although the Bush administration initially rejected attacking Iraq on September 15 and Bush later conceded Saddam Hussein had no role in 9/11, the attacks reshaped U.S. policy toward the subsequent invasion.

findings.claim: On September 11, 2001, 19 al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four commercial airliners, crashing two into the World Trade Center Twin Towers (which collapsed), one into the Pentagon, and a fourth—Flight 93—into a Pennsylvania field after passengers fought back.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial & Museum FAQs and National Park Service confirm the four coordinated hijackings by 19 al-Qaeda terrorists, the collapse of the Twin Towers, the Pentagon strike, and the Flight 93 passenger revolt.

evidence.quote: Nineteen terrorists from al-Qaeda hijacked four commercial airplanes, deliberately crashing two of the planes into the upper floors of the North and South Towers of the World Trade Center complex and a third plane into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia. The Twin Towers ultimately collapsed because of the damage sustained from the impacts and the resulting fires. After learning about the other attacks, passengers on the fourth hijacked plane, Flight 93, fought back, and the plane was crashed into an empty field in western Pennsylvania about 20 minutes by air from Washington, D.C.

findings.claim: The attacks killed 2,977 victims from 90 nations and targeted symbolic centers of American economic, military, and legislative power, triggering the October 2001 U.S. invasion of Afghanistan and sweeping counterterrorism and aviation security changes.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs confirm 2,977 victims from 90 nations, the symbolic targeting, and Operation Enduring Freedom; Wikipedia documents the worldwide counterterrorism legislation, the USA Patriot Act, DHS creation, and reinforced cockpits.

evidence.quote: The attacks killed 2,977 people from 90 nations: 2,753 people were killed in New York; 184 people were killed at the Pentagon; and 40 people were killed on Flight 93.
When they refused, “Operation Enduring Freedom” was launched on October 7, 2001, less than a month after the attacks of 9/11.
Many governments across the world passed legislation to combat terrorism as a result to the attacks.

findings.claim: American Airlines Flight 11 struck the North Tower at 8:46 a.m. and United Airlines Flight 175 struck the South Tower at 9:03 a.m.
findings.explanation: Both the 9/11 Memorial FAQs and Wikipedia record the exact impact times of 8:46 a.m. and 9:03 a.m.

evidence.quote: The hijacked Flight 11 was crashed into floors 93 to 99 of the North Tower (1 WTC) at 8:46 a.m. The hijacked Flight 175 struck floors 77 to 85 of the South Tower (2 WTC) 17 minutes later at 9:03 a.m.

findings.claim: Two hijacked Boeing 767s struck the Twin Towers, triggering jet-fuel fires that weakened the steel structures and caused both towers to collapse.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs and Wikipedia document the two strikes, structural damage, jet-fuel fires, and collapse of both towers.

evidence.quote: The fires from the impacts were intensified by the planes’ burning jet fuel. They weakened the steel support trusses, which attached each of the floors to the buildings’ exterior walls. Along with the initial damage to the buildings’ structural columns, this ultimately caused both towers to collapse.

findings.claim: Between 16,400 and 18,000 people were in the World Trade Center complex when the towers were hit; the vast majority evacuated safely, while 2,753 people were killed in New York and all five other buildings in the complex were destroyed.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs provide the exact occupancy range, evacuation outcome, destruction of the five other complex buildings, and New York victim count of 2,753.

evidence.quote: When the towers were struck, between 16,400 and 18,000 people were in the WTC complex. Of those, the vast majority evacuated safely. As they rushed out, first responders rushed in trying to save those still trapped or injured.
The five other buildings in the WTC complex were also destroyed because of damage sustained when the Twin Towers fell.
2,753 people were killed in New York; 184 people were killed at the Pentagon; and 40 people were killed on Flight 93.

findings.claim: American Airlines Flight 77 crashed into the Pentagon at 9:37 a.m.
findings.explanation: Both the National Park Service and Wikipedia confirm Flight 77 struck the Pentagon at 9:37 a.m.

evidence.quote: At 9:37 a.m. hijacked Flight 77 crashed into the Pentagon.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

findings.claim: Flight 77 struck the Pentagon's west wall, and minutes later the FAA ordered an unprecedented nationwide ground stop.
findings.explanation: Wikipedia documents the west-wall impact and fatalities, while the National Park Service documents the 9:45 a.m. FAA ground stop.

evidence.quote: The Federal Aviation Administration, at 9:45 a.m., ordered all aircraft to land at the nearest airport. An estimated 4,500 aircraft landed safely without incident. This was the first time such an order had been given in United States aviation history.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

findings.claim: American Airlines Flight 77 departed Dulles and struck the west wall of the Pentagon, killing 184 victims (59 passengers and crew plus 125 on the ground).
findings.explanation: Wikipedia's flight table gives 6 crew, 53 passengers, and 125 ground fatalities (totaling 184 victims plus 5 hijackers) at the west wall of the Pentagon, matching the 9/11 Memorial's figure of 184 victims killed at the Pentagon.

evidence.quote: American Airlines 77 Boeing 757–223[n] 8:20 a.m. 9:37 a.m. Washington Dulles International Airport Los Angeles International Airport West wall of Pentagon 6 53 125 5 189
184 people were killed at the Pentagon

findings.claim: United Airlines Flight 93 crashed in Pennsylvania at 10:03 a.m.
findings.explanation: The National Park Service and Wikipedia both record Flight 93 crashing at 10:03 a.m.

evidence.quote: At 10:03 a.m., Flight 93 plowed into an empty field at a speed of 563 miles per hour.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

findings.claim: Passengers and crew on Flight 93 learned of the earlier attacks by phone and launched a revolt that prevented the hijackers from reaching Washington, D.C.
findings.explanation: The National Park Service documents the airfone calls, the collective vote to fight back, and the crash in Pennsylvania.

evidence.quote: Using airfones, passengers and crew began making calls to report the hijacking. They soon learned the shocking news about the other hijacked planes and quickly realized that Flight 93 was part of a larger attack on America. This realization led to a vote and a collective decision to fight back.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

findings.claim: Delayed over 25 minutes out of Newark, Flight 93 had 33 passengers and 7 crew members who were hijacked around 9:28 a.m.; as they fought back, the hijackers rolled the plane upside down and chose to crash it into a Pennsylvania field.
findings.explanation: The National Park Service records the 25+ minute delay, the 33 passengers and 7 crew members, the 9:28 a.m. hijacking, the rolling maneuvers, and the deliberate crash.

evidence.quote: Seven crew members assigned to Flight 93 began to prepare for the early morning non-stop flight from Newark, New Jersey to San Francisco, California. Thirty-three passengers were traveling for ordinary reasons.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

evidence.quote: However, Flight 93 was delayed more than 25 minutes due to typically heavy morning traffic.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

evidence.quote: In its final moments, the plane turned upside down as it passed over rural Western Pennsylvania. The terrorists remained in control of the plane and chose to crash it rather than risk the passengers and crew regaining control of the aircraft.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

findings.claim: Operation Enduring Freedom began on October 7, 2001, and the Homeland Security Act passed in 2002.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs date Operation Enduring Freedom to October 7, 2001, and Wikipedia dates the Homeland Security Act to 2002.

evidence.quote: When they refused, “Operation Enduring Freedom” was launched on October 7, 2001, less than a month after the attacks of 9/11.
In the United States, the Department of Homeland Security was created by the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to coordinate domestic anti-terrorism efforts.

findings.claim: NATO invoked Article 5, the U.S. invaded Afghanistan after the Taliban refused to hand over al-Qaeda leaders, and Washington enacted the USA Patriot Act and created the Department of Homeland Security.
findings.explanation: Wikipedia and the 9/11 Memorial FAQs document NATO's Article 5 declaration, the ultimatum to the Taliban, the USA Patriot Act, and the creation of DHS.

evidence.quote: The NATO council declared that the terrorist attacks on the United States were an attack on all NATO nations that satisfied Article 5 of the NATO charter.

The USA Patriot Act gave the federal government greater powers, including the authority to detain foreign terror suspects for a week without charge; to monitor terror suspects' telephone communications, e-mail, and Internet use; and to prosecute suspected terrorists without time restrictions.

findings.claim: President Bush demanded the Taliban surrender al-Qaeda and close training camps, launching Operation Enduring Freedom when they refused; domestically, the FAA ordered reinforced cockpits and sky marshals.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs detail the U.S. ultimatum to the Taliban and Bush's September 20, 2001 speech; Wikipedia records the FAA cockpit reinforcement order and sky marshals.

evidence.quote: The U.S. government insisted that the Taliban immediately hand over the terrorists and close the training camps or face an attack from the United States.
The FAA ordered that airplane cockpits be reinforced with a secondary flight deck to prevent terrorists from gaining control of planes and assigned sky marshals to flights.

findings.claim: After subways and tunnels closed on 9/11, an improvised flotilla of ferries, tugboats, charter vessels, fireboats, and private boats answered a U.S. Coast Guard call and evacuated an estimated 300,000 to 500,000 people from Lower Manhattan in less than nine hours, the largest waterborne evacuation in American history.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial & Museum and Smithsonian Magazine independently corroborate the makeshift maritime boatlift of ferries, tugboats, and private/commercial vessels evacuating 300,000 to 500,000 people from Lower Manhattan after subways and tunnels shut down.

evidence.quote: Seeing the emergency, the U.S. Coast Guard issued a call for all available boats to help those who were trapped. The ensuing maritime response, from NYPD harbor units, fireboats and ferries to private and commercial boats, initiated the largest waterborne evacuation in American history.
evidence.origin: National September 11 Memorial & Museum, All Available Boats

evidence.quote: they reflect on 9/11 and the improvised evacuation that transported an estimated 300,000 to 500,000 people to safety in less than nine hours.
evidence.origin: National September 11 Memorial & Museum, All Available Boats

evidence.quote: A makeshift armada of about 150 commercial vessels of various types—tugboats, ferries, charter boats—would transport an estimated 500,000 people out of the disaster zone of lower Manhattan to safety in New Jersey and Brooklyn.
evidence.origin: Smithsonian Magazine, On 9/11, a Flotilla of Ferries, Yachts and Tugboats Evacuated 500,000 People Away From Ground Zero

evidence.quote: Subways had screeched to a stop. The tunnels underneath the Hudson were closed.
evidence.origin: Smithsonian Magazine, On 9/11, a Flotilla of Ferries, Yachts and Tugboats Evacuated 500,000 People Away From Ground Zero

findings.claim: Following the unprecedented 9:45 a.m. FAA ground stop that landed roughly 4,500 aircraft in the U.S., Canada's Operation Yellow Ribbon shut Canadian airspace for the first time and diverted 225 to 240 international flights to 17 airports, including 38 airliners with 6,122 passengers and 473 crew in Gander, Newfoundland.
findings.explanation: The U.S. National Park Service and Wikipedia's Operation Yellow Ribbon article independently corroborate the unprecedented FAA ground stop, and Wikipedia details the Canadian diversion totals and Gander's 38 airliners.

evidence.quote: The Federal Aviation Administration, at 9:45 a.m., ordered all aircraft to land at the nearest airport. An estimated 4,500 aircraft landed safely without incident. This was the first time such an order had been given in United States aviation history.
evidence.origin: U.S. National Park Service, Flight 93 National Memorial

evidence.quote: Canada commenced the operation after the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), implementing Security Control of Air Traffic and Air Navigation Aids (SCATANA), grounded all aircraft across the United States, an unprecedented action.
In total, as a result of Operation Yellow Ribbon, between 225 and 240 aircraft were diverted to 17 different airports across the country.
Gander International Airport in Newfoundland, Canada, played host to 38 airliners, totaling 6,122 passengers and 473 crew, as part of Operation Yellow Ribbon.

findings.claim: Recovered from the World Trade Center rubble in October 2001 as a badly burned 8-foot Callery pear with snapped roots and one living branch, the Survivor Tree was rehabilitated by NYC Parks in the Bronx, survived a March 2010 storm uprooting, and returned to the 9/11 Memorial in December 2010 at 30 feet tall with smooth new limbs extending from gnarled stumps.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial & Museum and Wikipedia's National September 11 Memorial & Museum article independently corroborate the Callery pear's October 2001 discovery, its Bronx NYC Parks rehabilitation, and its 2010 return to the Memorial.

evidence.quote: In October 2001, a severely damaged tree was discovered at Ground Zero, with snapped roots and burned and broken branches. The tree was removed from the rubble and placed in the care of the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation. After its recovery and rehabilitation, the tree was returned to the Memorial in 2010. New, smooth limbs extended from the gnarled stumps, creating a visible demarcation between the tree’s past and present.
evidence.origin: National September 11 Memorial & Museum, The Survivor Tree

evidence.quote: When the 8-foot (2.4 m)-tall tree was recovered,[59] it was badly burned and had one living branch.
evidence.origin: English Wikipedia, National September 11 Memorial & Museum

evidence.quote: Still under the care of the Bronx nursery, the tree was replanted without significant damage in March 2010 after it was uprooted by a storm.
evidence.origin: English Wikipedia, National September 11 Memorial & Museum

evidence.quote: In December 2010, the tree, then 30 feet (9.1 m) tall,[58] was returned to the World Trade Center site
evidence.origin: English Wikipedia, National September 11 Memorial & Museum

findings.claim: Osama bin Laden founded and led al-Qaeda, which carried out the 9/11 attacks, and was killed in a U.S. military operation on May 1, 2011.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs and Wikipedia identify Osama bin Laden as al-Qaeda's founder and leader and date his death in a U.S. operation to May 1, 2011.

evidence.quote: Al-Qaeda is an international Islamist extremist terrorist network founded in the late 1980s by Osama bin Laden, who was killed in a U.S. military operation on May 1, 2011, and others who were involved in the war against the Soviet Union in Afghanistan.

findings.claim: President George W. Bush told Congress on September 20, 2001, that any nation harboring or supporting terrorism would be treated as a hostile regime, leading to Operation Enduring Freedom.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs quote Bush's September 20, 2001 address to Congress and link it directly to the October 7, 2001 invasion of Afghanistan.

evidence.quote: On September 20, 2001, in a speech to a joint session of Congress, former President George W. Bush asserted: “Any nation that continues to harbor or support terrorism will be regarded by the United States as a hostile regime.”

findings.claim: Operation Enduring Freedom began in Afghanistan on October 7, 2001, because the Taliban harbored al-Qaeda and refused U.S. demands to hand over the terrorists.
findings.explanation: The 9/11 Memorial FAQs directly link al-Qaeda's safe haven under the Taliban to the October 7, 2001 launch of Operation Enduring Freedom.

evidence.quote: Al-Qaeda was based in Afghanistan. They operated training camps there, and openly lived in the country with the support of the Taliban, an Islamist group that ruled the country.
When they refused, “Operation Enduring Freedom” was launched on October 7, 2001, less than a month after the attacks of 9/11.

findings.claim: At Camp David on September 15, 2001, the Bush administration rejected attacking Iraq over 9/11, yet later invaded citing Saddam Hussein's support for terrorism before Bush conceded three years later that Hussein played no role in the attacks.
findings.explanation: Wikipedia documents the September 15 Camp David decision, the subsequent invasion of Iraq, and Bush's later concession that Saddam Hussein had no role in 9/11.

evidence.quote: In a meeting at Camp David on September 15 the Bush administration rejected the idea of attacking Iraq in response to the September 11 attacks.[312] Nonetheless, they later invaded the country with allies, citing "Saddam Hussein's support for terrorism."[313] At the time, as many as seven in ten Americans believed the Iraqi president played a role in the 9/11 attacks.[314] Three years later, Bush conceded that he had not.
